messages:
maya: FYI starting a key-migration backfill tonight to rotate DEKs encrypted under alias/old-key -> alias/new-key. plan: fanout via SQS -> batch workers in us-west-2, with regional fallbacks. window 00:00-06:00 PDT. any blockers?

alex: +1 on window. main risk is hitting KMS throttling during peak. we should token-bucket throttle per-worker and per-account.

jon: also watch audit logs — need entry for every rewrap action and the invoking principal. set CloudTrail + SIEM ingestion for the job id.

maya: agreed. using KMS ReEncrypt where available (AWS) to avoid plaintext in our workers. for GCP/Azure we may need decrypt/encrypt flow so we'll spin ephemeral workers in respective cloud and limit parallelism.

priya: can we avoid plaintext on cross-cloud? any provider supports server-side rewrap to a different provider?

alex: no cross-cloud server-side rewrap afaik. options: 1) perform re-encrypt in a trusted ephemeral container holding DEK in memory only, strict mlock, no swap, short life; 2) rotate customer envelope keys by adding a new wrapping key and update pointers without touching ciphertext if supported. but for migrating between KMS vendors you need plaintext DEK at some point.

jon: important: RBAC change — create a new role "key-migration-runner" with just kms:ReEncrypt / kms:GenerateDataKey / cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt (vendor mapped). avoid giving broad decrypt/unwrap to general ops. runbooks must require two approvers for production runs.

maya: good call. infra-sre: can you add the role and a short policy draft?

infra-sre: adding now. policy draft: allow: kms:ReEncrypt on aliases/new-key and aliases/old-key, kms:DescribeKey, logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents for job-*; deny: kms:CreateGrant. will push to iam repo and request audit.

kms-bot: Job 37621 started: backfill-wave-1 (workers=40, concurrency-per-worker=2). monitoring: /dashboards/kms/backfill/37621

maya: quick note on idempotency: worker should include a checkpoint per-ciphertext id and a compare-and-swap update to mark rotated=true. use optimistic retries: if update fails because already rotated, treat success.

alex: on errors, push to DLQ with failure_reason + last_attempt_ts + stacktrace. we should also capture original ciphertext length/hash to detect corruption.

priya: rate-limit plan: start at 20% of observed KMS QPS, ramp every 10 minutes by 20% until we see increased 5xx from KMS or elevated latency >200ms. if throttle triggers, backoff exponential with jitter and reduce global concurrency by 30%.

jon: add a safety cutoff: if error-rate > 1% for 15m, pause job and notify oncall; require manual resume after investigation.

maya: ops checklist before run: 1) IAM role created, 2) dashboard + alerts, 3) DLQ subscription and retention 30d, 4) dry-run on 100 keys in staging, 5) runbook for resume + rollback.

infra-sre: done for IAM and dashboards. DLQ subscription configured (pager on >10 failures/min).

kms-bot: Job 37621 progress: 1200/48000 items processed (2.5%), 9 failures -> DLQ. current worker qps 210, average KMS latency 85ms.

maya: good to validate the 9 failures quickly — likely transient KMS throttles. jon/infra-sre can you check logs and either requeue or adjust throttles?

jon: looking. the first failure is KMS.InternalServerError from us-east-1; will requeue with increased jitter. marking job 37621 attempt++ for those ids.

priya: remember audit: every successful re-encrypt must be correlated to original ciphertext id in CloudTrail so we can reconstruct history for compliance. include job-id and operator principal in the log entry.

alex: also ensure encryption context is preserved during re-encrypt. don't drop metadata fields. failing that, fail the item.

maya: after run we'll produce a compliance artifact: CSV with key_id, object_id, old_key, new_key, timestamp, job_id, operator. keep that in S3 with SSE-KMS and restricted ACLs.

infra-sre: question on backfill resume: workers will checkpoint last_processed_id per-shard in DynamoDB. on resume they scan for not-rotated ids. ensure scan page size limit so resume won't hot-scan table.

jon: propose also building a resumable cursor file per shard with sequence token and last_cursor_ts. store with encryption and TTL.

maya: agreed. final ask: security team sign-off on runbook and RBAC before start. I'll wait for thumbs-up and then kickoff dry-run at 02:00 PDT.

priya: thumbs-up from me once runbook pushed to /docs/runbooks/kms-migration.md.

alex: +1 — I'll monitor metrics during dry-run.

infra-sre: IAM PR merged, runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-migration, pager rota updated.

kms-bot: Job 37621 dry-run complete: 100 items processed, 0 failures. awaiting prod approval.

maya: thanks. tagging @security-leads for final approval :eyes:
